summary: Petition under Sections 79(1)(c), 79(1)(f) and 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the CERC Office Order dated 30.07.2025, Addendum dated 14.01.2026 issued by this Commission, Committee Report dated 05.01.2026, Regulations 13(2)(h), 27 and 28 of the CERC (Sharing on Inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2020 and Regulations 42 and 44 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 for seeking Extension of Time in SCOD for the Petitioner’s project. **Ambuja Cements Limited** Adani Corporate House, Shantigram, S.G. Highway, Khodiyar, Ahmedabad – 382421, Gujarat, India ** Petitioner** Shri Anshu Deshpande, Advocate, ACL Shri Shubham Arya, Advocate, CTUIL Ms. Pallavi Saigal, Advocate, CTUIL Ms. Harsha Parakh, Advocate, CTUIL The present Petition has been filed by Ambuja Cements Limited (hereinafter referred to as the “Petitioner”/ “ACL”) seeking extension of Scheduled Commercial Operation Date (“SCOD”) for the Petitioner’s project under Regulation 13(2)(h) of the CERC (Sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2020 (hereinafter referred to as the “2020 Sharing Regulations”). The Petitioner has made the following prayers: - _(b) Waive 100% of the ISTS charges associated with the Petitioner’s Project on account of extension of SCOD;_ - _(c) Pass such order and further order or orders as this Hon’ble Commission deems appropriate under the facts and circumstances of the present case._ - (k) Since the delay in achieving COD arose solely due to factors beyond the control of the Petitioner, the Petitioner is entitled to the 100% waiver of the ISTS charges. **4.** The learned counsel for the CTUIL submitted that it adopts the recommendations of the Committee and does not wish to file any separate reply in the matter. The Commission directed the Petitioner to implead the concerned Solar Power Park, i.e., ESUCRL, as a party to the Petition and file a revised memo of parties within a week and file the following information: (iii) Documents substantiating the delay in completion of facilities of ESUCRL's solar power park on account of force majeure events claimed in the instant Petition. (iii) Details of force majeure events claimed by the Petitioner for the delay of ESUCRL's solar power park in the instant Petition, as per the following table: **6.** The Petitioner has filed amended memo of parties on 21.05.2026 impleading ESUCRL as a party to the instant Petition. # ** Submissions of Petitioner in Compliance with the RoP for hearing dated 13.05.2026: ** **7.** The Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 01.06.2026, re-iterated its earlier submissions and has mainly submitted as under: - (b) The Letter dated 27.06.2025 from the MNRE to ESUCRL granting the extension till 30.09.2025 explicitly records that the said extension is being granted for “pending activities: line charging of PSS and final commissioning”. Prior to this, MNRE granted an extension till 31.12.2024 vide letter dated 24.09.2024. - (c) The Petitioner has furnished the copy of NRLDC Approval (Form-IV) dated 07.07.2025 granting permission for charging and trial operation of the relevant facilities at ESUCRL’s Main Pooling Sub-Station. Pursuant to the said approval, ESUCRL successfully charged the Pooling Station on 08.07.2025. - (d) The Petitioner has also submitted a copy of ESUCRL’s communication dated 24.12.2024, addressed to MNRE, setting out, inter alia, the force majeure circumstances affecting the development and completion of the Solar Park and seeking extension of timelines. ||||delay in allotment of land pursuant to this litigation)| |---|---|---|---| |5.|31.03.2024|31.12.2024|MNRE’s letter dated 24.09.2024 in response to Essel Saurya’s letter dated 24.04.2024 and email dated 12.08.2024 extending commissioning timeline for Essel’s Solar Park to 31.12.2024.| |6.|31.12.2024|30.09.2025|MNRE’s letter dated 27.06.2025 in response to Essel Saurya’s letters dated 24.12.2024, 08.05.2025 and 08.06.2025 (requesting an extension on account of status quo orders and delay in allotment of land pursuant to this litigation).| |7.|30.09.2025|31.03.2029|MNRE’s OM dated 17.09.2025 extending the timeline for the completion of ongoing Solar Parks awarded under MNRE’s Solar Park scheme OM No. 30/26/2014-15-NSM (Essel Saurya was also awarded the project under this scheme) for a period of 3 years without any additional financial implication, for completion of the ongoing parks and clearing committed liabilities. This OM is marked to all Solar Power Park Developers.| **9.** The Commission directed the ESUCRL to submit the date of charging of the Park Pooling Station, where the Petitioner’s project was to be connected, along with the supporting document and the internal evacuation arrangement of the park and how the force majeure event has impacted the COD of the Petitioner project. The Commission also reserved the matter for orders. - (c) As regards the impact of the Force Majeure events on the COD of Petitioner’s project, the Petitioner’s project was dependent upon the common infrastructure of the ESUCRL’s Solar Park, including the pooling station and evacuation system. The development and completion of such infrastructure were delayed due to various Force Majeure events and circumstances beyond ESUCRL’s control. **11.** We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and the Respondents, and the documents placed on the record. The following issue arises for our consideration: **19.** In view of the above discussions, we are of the considered view that the Petitioner’s project shall be eligible for waiver of inter-state transmission charges, as if the project had achieved COD on or before 30.06.2025 in terms of Regulation 13(2)(h) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations.
